service.description:
The host name this website gets on THIS installation: the first label of its own domain, on the domain this backend is reached at. www.xxxx.com becomes xxxx.growerp.org.
Follows the same rule as setup#MainOrganization: a host with two or more dots loses its first label, so admin/staging prefixes do not end up in the name. Returns empty when there is no web request (a background job), the caller then keeps what it has.

parameter.name: sourceHostName
parameter.description: domain of the website, eg www.antwebsystems.com

parameter.description: month the accounting year starts in: any month 1..12

parameter.name: hostNames
parameter.description: comma separated; when empty they are derived from the source url

return.message: Fiscal year start month: ${fiscalYearStartMonth} should be a month 1..12

service.description: Write the progress of a conversion in its own transaction, so the page sees it immediately and a later failure cannot roll the progress back.

Background worker: scrape the source site, generate the pages and theme with AI, then install everything as a new owner. Every step commits its progress through update#WebsiteConversionStatus so the support app can follow along.
Read a public website with Jsoup; input for generate#WebsiteContent.
Turn scraped website data into an owner-import XML document with Gemini.

Install an owner-import XML that was exported here or produced by the /convert-website skill, and record it in the conversion list. The file carries its own ownerSpec.json, so only the file itself is needed.
Runs inline rather than in the background: an import is database work only, it takes seconds, unlike a conversion which reads a website and calls an AI.

parameter.name: password
parameter.description: login password for the new owner, generated when left empty

return.message: This is not a GrowERP website export: no <ID>_ROOT resource found in the file

service.description: Rebuild the owner-import XML of a website that is live here, so it can be installed on another GrowERP with import#WebsiteOwner. Reads the current content, so later edits made in the admin app's Website dialog are included. Works for any website, whether the generator, the /convert-website skill or a person made it.

parameter.name: productStoreId
parameter.description: the store to export; either this or conversionId

parameter.description: id prefix for the generated file, default from the company name

parameter.name: adminEmail
parameter.description: login for the target installation; left empty it has to be filled in before the file can be imported

return.message: Conversion ${conversionId} has no finished website to export
Either productStoreId or conversionId is required
